title: AI Routing Explained: The Design Pattern Every AI Engineer Needs | Trail 1 · Lesson 12
description:
Your support bot answers an invoice question in the upbeat tone of the sales team. The model isn't broken. One prompt is trying to be five specialists at once.

In this lesson you'll learn routing, the design pattern that splits deciding from answering: a small, cheap model classifies each message, plain code picks the path, and each path gets its own short prompt and only its own tools. Anything uncertain goes to a person.

What you'll learn:
• Why one giant system prompt degrades every topic it covers
• How to classify intent with a small model and structured output
• Why the routing decision belongs in code, not in the prompt
• How a confidence threshold handles messages with two topics
• What to measure in production, and why a route is not access control
